title: TFI Earnings Beat: Is This Stock the Freight Recovery King?
author: Jeffrey Neal Johnson
description: TFI International delivered strong Q1 results suggesting a cyclical bottom in the freight sector. The company's LTL segment showed dramatic volume recovery with March volumes up 8% YoY, and management expects 400-500 basis points of sequential OR improvement in Q2. The Truckload division demonstrated disciplined fleet management with 8.6% revenue per truck growth while reducing truck count by 7.1%. Despite strong performance, management withheld full-year guidance due to USMCA trade agreement uncertainty in July 2026. The stock reached a 52-week high with a 35% YTD return, and Bank of America upgraded it to Buy with a $161 price target.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company demonstrated strong Q1 earnings beat with significant volume recovery in LTL segment (8% YoY growth in March), disciplined operational management (8.6% revenue per truck growth while reducing fleet size), and aggressive Q2 guidance (400-500 bps OR improvement). Management raised dividend by 4% despite lower FCF, signaling confidence in future cash flows. Stock reached 52-week high with 35% YTD return and received Bank of America upgrade to Buy with $161 price target. Primary risk is USMCA trade agreement review in July 2026.

title: TFI International Declares Quarterly Dividend
author: Globe Newswire
description: TFI International Inc. announced a quarterly dividend of US $0.47 per common share, payable on April 15, 2026 to shareholders of record as of March 31, 2026. The company is a North American leader in transportation and logistics operating across the US, Canada, and Mexico.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The declaration of a quarterly dividend demonstrates financial strength and confidence in the company's cash flow generation. Regular dividend payments are typically viewed positively by investors as they indicate stable profitability and management's commitment to returning value to shareholders.

title: TFI Delivering Rapid Data Center Related Growth
author: Na
description: TFI International reported significant growth in its data center and electric grid-related transportation business, with data center revenue growing from $8 million in Q1 to $15 million in Q4 2025. The company appointed Scott Hoppe as Chief Commercial Officer of its SFI truckload brand to capitalize on the expanding data center buildout across North America.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company demonstrated strong revenue growth in its data center business (87.5% quarterly growth from Q1 to Q4 2025), broad electric grid revenue exceeding $110 million, and strategic leadership appointment to capitalize on early-stage data center industry expansion. Management expressed confidence in significant future opportunities in this high-growth sector.

title: TFI International Declares Quarterly Dividend

description: TFI International announced a quarterly dividend of US $0.47 per outstanding common share, representing a 4% increase from the previous dividend, payable on January 15, 2026 to shareholders of record by December 31, 2025.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company increased quarterly dividend by 4%, indicating financial strength and confidence in future performance

title: Dixon Mitchell Investment Counsel Adds Another $7 Million of TFI International Stock on the Dip
author: Josh Kohn-Lindquist
description: Investment firm Dixon Mitchell increased its stake in TFI International by 93,705 shares, valued at approximately $7 million, despite the stock being 36% below its 52-week highs, indicating confidence in the transportation and logistics company's long-term potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite stock price decline, Dixon Mitchell is buying more shares, suggesting strong belief in the company's fundamentals, growth potential, and attractive valuation at current levels
